findings.failure_mode: Any I/O error (missing file, permissions, disk full, ENOMEM) panics the thread instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return a typed error (e.g. io::Error mapped via map_err or a domain Io error variant) from load_shards

findings.failure_mode: Non-numeric or out-of-range payload text in column 2 panics the thread instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ParseError::Invalid) and propagate via a Fallible return

findings.problem: as u16 lossy cast from u32 parse result
findings.failure_mode: A u32 value > 65535 silently truncates to u16, silently corrupting data with no error reported
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) to reject values outside u16 range

findings.failure_mode: A line with fewer than 1 comma-separated field panics via index out of bounds
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) and pattern-match the two parts

findings.failure_mode: A line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields panics via index out of bounds
findings.fix: Use split_once to get name and value_str simultaneously; never index into a split result

findings.problem: println!() inside load_shards — logging in core logic
findings.failure_mode: Side effects in the pure computation path prevent deterministic testing, cause log pollution in consumers, and violate the functional core / imperative shell separation
findings.fix: Remove println! from load_shards; emit log events only in the imperative shell layer after the core returns

findings.problem: load_shards performs raw I/O (fs::read_to_string) and logging, mixing shell duties into the core
findings.failure_mode: The core is not testable without real filesystem access; side effects are uncontrolled; the function cannot be used in async or mocked contexts
findings.fix: Split into a pure core parse_records(&[RecordInput]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> and a shell layer load_shards(path) that handles I/O and delegates to the core

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 — no newtypes, no domain invariants, no typestate
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct a Record with an empty name, a negative value (if signed), or any invalid combination; illegal states are representable
findings.fix: Define Name(String) or Newtype with a fallible constructor that enforces non-empty; use a typed error; consider an enum typestate if lifecycle is relevant

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String, u32) enter the domain via unvalidated split and collect; no smart constructor or parse boundary
findings.failure_mode: Callers can bypass all validation by constructing Record directly or by passing arbitrary strings through split
findings.fix: Parse at the boundary into newtype/enum variants through fallible constructors; do not expose raw primitives in the domain

findings.problem: Collects all split parts into Vec<String> without any capacity reservation or item limit
findings.failure_mode: A single malformed line with many commas can trigger unbounded heap allocation; the function has no max-items guard and no try_reserve
findings.fix: Use split_once instead of collect; if multi-field parsing is needed, enforce a max_fields bound and use try_reserve before collecting

findings.problem: load_shards returns Vec<Record> with no error type — all failures are panics via unwrap
findings.failure_mode: No consumer can distinguish I/O failure from parse failure from overflow; the error taxonomy is entirely absent
findings.fix: Define an enum ParseError { Io(io::Error), Invalid, Overflow } and return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: use std::fs; imported at top level — I/O module visible throughout the crate
findings.failure_mode: Any function in the crate can import std::fs and perform I/O, eroding the functional core / imperative shell boundary
findings.fix: Move std::fs usage to the shell module; core should have no std::fs import

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_shards throughput or latency
no profiler data (perf, flamegraph) for the hot path
no allocation audit (no try_reserve, no capacity tracking on the Vec)
no second-ring evidence (Kani, Miri, proptest) for parse boundary invariants
no command evidence (cargo test, cargo fmt, cargo clippy) was executed — static review only
no workload characterization (expected line counts, field counts, error rates)
residual_risk: Static review only — no commands run. All I/O, parse, casting, and allocation paths are unsafe without verified execution. The crate as written would panic on any malformed input or I/O error, silently truncate u32 values via as u16, and cannot be tested deterministically due to embedded println! and fs::read_to_string in the core.
